subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Vitamin C is essential for immune function and collagen production in the human body.
• Vitamin C is a nutrient found in various fruits.
• Oranges contain 53 milligrams per 100 grams (mg/100g) of vitamin C.
• Strawberries contain 89 mg/100g.
• Kiwi fruit contains 155 mg/100g.
prompt: The student wants to identify which of the three fruits has the highest vitamin C content. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Kiwi fruit contains 155 mg/100g of vitamin C, which is more than oranges and strawberries.
choices.B: At 89 mg/100g, strawberries contain more vitamin C than oranges (53 mg/100g).
choices.C: Vitamin C is found in various fruits, including oranges, strawberries, and kiwi fruit.
choices.D: Oranges contain 53 mg/100g of vitamin C, a nutrient essential for immune function and collagen production.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence identifies kiwi fruit as having the highest vitamin C content of the three fruits, noting that they contain 155 mg/100g, which is more than both oranges and strawberries.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The sentence compares the vitamin C content of strawberries and oranges; it doesn't identify which of the three fruits has the highest vitamin C content.
